title: A senior case is timeboxed at 6h and the candidate is told so up front
expected: A brief, <30-min real case that respects his level (research anchor: long take-homes lose 40-60% of strong seniors).
got: design.py hardcodes _TIMEBOX = {junior:3, medior:4, senior:6, lead:8}; design_case fits the work to ~6h for a senior and writes timeboxHours into the case. caseToMarkdown then renders it verbatim as '~6h timebox' in the brief Sam reads. A 6-hour take-home is exactly the multi-hour grind Sam declines — he walks the instant he sees it.
l2_priority: Author a REAL senior need and read the live brief: is the surfaced timebox 6h (or whatever the LLM emits)? Does the brief read like a half-day take-home? Time how long the actual scoped work would take a senior. The brevity gate (devcase-constraints.ts only caps MAX_CODEBASES=3) does NOT bound case scope — confirm whether any guard keeps a senior case short.
suggested_acceptance: A senior dev case presents a timebox of <=2h (ideally a <30-min focused slice) and the brief reads as a brief real task, not a half-day take-home.

title: Two contradictory submit paths on one page: work in-product OR paste a repo URL
expected: One coherent way to do the work and submit it. If the product observes my process in-browser, that should be THE submission.
got: The page renders the LiveWorkSurface in-product editor (submits observed process via /api/devcase/session/[id]/submit) AND, directly below, a DevApplyForm headed 'Submit your solution' whose 'Solution repository URL' field is REQUIRED and whose hint says 'Push your work to a public repository and share the link'. The two models contradict: if I work in the in-browser editor, what repo URL do I paste? The workSurface error copy even points me to 'the repository-link option below', conceding the editor is secondary. As a senior I can't tell which path is real or whether my in-editor work even counts.
l2_priority: Open a real token: do BOTH surfaces render together? Submit via the editor — does it complete WITHOUT a repo URL? Then is the required-repo DevApplyForm still demanding a URL? Confirm whether a candidate who only used the editor can finish, and whether one submission or two get created.
suggested_acceptance: The candidate sees ONE submission path. If the live-work editor is present, the repo-link form is hidden or clearly framed as an alternative for those who worked locally; the in-product submission completes without requiring a GitHub URL.

title: The live-work 'editor' is a bare textarea with no run/execute
expected: A live-work surface that doesn't fight me — ideally I can run/verify the code I edit, since the case grades verification.
got: LiveWorkSurface is a single monospace <textarea> over the seed files (no syntax highlighting, no language server, no runner/test execution). It loads, accepts input, and saves observed events on an 8s flush — so it functionally works and won't lag. But the case explicitly rewards verification (verification_trap probe), and there is no way IN the surface to run anything or prove a change is safe — I'd have to do that work elsewhere, which reopens the repo-URL path. For a senior, a textarea is a downgrade from any real editor.
l2_priority: Drive the editor live: does it stay responsive on a multi-KB file? Does selecting/editing files reliably register observed events (open/edit/decision_log)? Confirm the absence of any run/test affordance and whether the brief asks the candidate to verify without giving them a way to.
suggested_acceptance: The live-work surface is responsive and saves reliably; if the case asks for verification, the surface offers a way to run/test (or the brief is explicit that verification is described, not executed).

title: The eval grades human-AI judgment from MY observed process, not leetcode recall
expected: Judge how I collaborate with AI and where I override it, not whether I memorized an algorithm.
got: The whole pipeline assumes code is 100% LLM-generated (design._SYSTEM, evaluate._SYSTEM) and grades five durable capabilities (framing, tooling, judgment, architecture, transfer) from the observed reflection + probe outcomes, never correctness/volume. mint_followups anchors interview questions to MY specific observed decisions (which defensible option I shipped at each probe) and treats the scores as hypotheses to verify live. submission_eval gates fairness (verification rewarded, AI use NOT penalised) and discrimination. This is exactly the AI-era judgment signal Sam wants — a clear senior-quality strength to protect.
l2_priority: With a key present, confirm a live eval cites HIS observed events (files touched, DECISIONS.md, probe path) and the verdict reads evidence-backed, not a generic grade.

title: The candidate brief is probe-safe by construction (no answer-key leak)
expected: A real case where the interesting part is hidden judgment, not a leaked rubric I could game.
got: The page renders caseToMarkdown (title/brief/tasks only) and NEVER the raw case object; coverProbes, reveals, decisionSpace and rubric weights are excluded by construction. A senior can't reverse-engineer what's being tested — the ambiguity stays the instrument.
l2_priority: Inspect the live page source/markdown: confirm no probe text, reveals, or rubric weight leaks into the candidate DOM.

title: The dev-case page carries no AI-use disclosure even though AI evaluates the submission
expected: As an engineer I want to know plainly: is AI assessing my submission, and does a human still decide?
got: The /apply chat mounts <AiDisclosure showDataConsent /> (AI assists, a human decides, 12-month retention, erasure link). The /devcase/apply/[token] page mounts NO AiDisclosure at all — yet this is the surface where an LLM pipeline (evaluate.py) actually scores the work and mints interview questions. The workSurface intro mentions 'we grade the judgment we watch' and 'You may use any tools, including AI' but never discloses that AI evaluates HIM, nor a GDPR/retention/erasure line. For Sam (trust is an explicit scored criterion) that absence is a major gap on the exact surface where AI acts on him.
l2_priority: Open the live token page and confirm no AI/GDPR disclosure renders anywhere on the dev-case apply surface; confirm the apply chat's disclosure does render, to verify the gap is dev-case-specific.

title: Apply returns a real status token and a self-serve timeline (no ghosting)
expected: Apply in English, then SEE where I stand without emailing anyone.
got: On accept, the apply route mints a status link (getOrCreateStatusLink) and ConversationalApply renders a 'Track your application status' button to /status/[token]. The status page shows received -> under review -> interview -> offer -> hired with a current-step 'now' line, plus honest terminal not-selected/withdrawn cards. This directly answers Sam's no-ghosting requirement.
l2_priority: Apply against a real seeded job, follow the returned token, and confirm the live stage matches the recruiter pipeline (token-mint fixture is the blocker).

title: Apply: explicit AI/human disclosure + GDPR consent, in natively fluent English
expected: Tell me plainly AI reads my application and a human still decides; don't dark-pattern consent; don't machine-translate the UI.
got: AiDisclosure on the apply chat states 'A human reviews and makes every advance, offer, and rejection decision; nothing adverse is decided automatically. You can ask for a human review at any point' plus a 12-month retention + erasure-link consent line; submitting IS the consent (no pre-ticked box). The en.json copy across apply/status/devApply reads as native-fluent English (idiomatic em-dashes, contractions, no machine-translation tells). Both Sam's clarity and trust criteria pass on the apply leg.
l2_priority: Confirm en locale renders with no leaked Czech strings and the consent line is visible at the point of submit.

title: Status leg is unreachable at L1 without a minted token fixture
expected: A status link I can open.
got: /status/[token] resolves entirely by token (env.md open question #3 — local mint path unresolved). The DESIGNED path is sound (token returned on apply, see sam-cas-01), but L1 cannot confirm reachability. Tagged unreachable; defer job-impact verdict to L2 once the token fixture exists.
l2_priority: Resolve the token-mint path (apply returns one in the POST response — capture it) and confirm /status/[token] opens and shows the live stage.
